approved: Coal Mining Industry (Long Service Leave) Legislation Amendment Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would allow employers in the black coal mining industry to voluntarily set up payment plans for long service leave levies they have not paid in the past.
It would replace the outdated method for calculating interest on late levy payments with a rate tied to the Reserve Bank of Australia's cash rate target.
Employers who enter a 6-year instalment plan could get 20% of their debt waived once they pay 80%, and would not face legal action or extra levy during the period.
The bill creates a voluntary instalment process for overdue long service leave levies.
It updates how additional levy is calculated for late payments to use the RBA cash rate.
It allows the Corporation to create employee service records using reasonable assumptions when employer records are incomplete.
Employers in the black coal mining industry who have disputed employee eligibility and owe past levies, and their eligible employees.

Moved the second reading of the Coal Mining Industry (Long Service Leave) Legislation Amendment Bill 2025, arguing that it would give eligible black coal mining workers access to full long service leave entitlements while providing employers with a pathway to settle historical levy debts through instalments over six years and a 20 per cent waiver after 80 per cent is paid.

Supported the Coal Mining Industry (Long Service Leave) Legislation Amendment Bill 2025, which provides eligible employers a voluntary pathway to repay historical levy debts over six years after 80 per cent is paid, with the remaining 20 per cent waived and penalties stopped, while speakers said it would protect workers' entitlements and reduce business risks.

Supported the Coal Mining Industry (Long Service Leave) Legislation Amendment Bill 2025, arguing that staged repayment of historical unpaid levies would protect worker entitlements, employer viability and coal-region economies; the bill was read a second time.

Tabled revised explanatory memoranda and moved several bills for second reading. The measures would create a payment pathway for historical coal mining long-service-leave levies, reform secrecy offences by removing criminal liability from more than 300 provisions while protecting press freedom, and adjust Pension Supplement payments for temporary and permanent overseas absences.

Moved that the Coal Mining Industry (Long Service Leave) Legislation Amendment Bill 2026 be considered at 12.15 pm, government business continue until no later than 1.30 pm, and general business notice of motion no. 558 be considered that day; the question was agreed to.

Moved an amendment calling for immediate pursuit of backpay for casual coal mine workers allegedly underpaid through labour hire contracts, while supporting the bill's voluntary pathway for employers to resolve historical unpaid levies. Argued the measure balances workers' entitlements with business viability through staged repayments and a 20 per cent waiver; the minister said a Fair Work Ombudsman investigation was ongoing.
